title: A Yearbook for the Homecoming
premise: Silas Voss, a scholarship student at Hollowmere Academy, is paired with his tormentor Wren Calloway for a senior project: documenting the town's fading Homecoming tradition. Digging through the academy's archives, they uncover that the original Homecoming was a memorial for students who died in a fire the school erased from every record—including one bearing Silas's own surname. As the administration moves to cancel Homecoming and bury the truth forever, Silas and Wren must decide whether justice means exposure or restoration; in the end, they rebuild the tradition as an honest memorial, Silas chooses to stay in Hollowmere rather than flee it, and the town finally speaks its dead aloud.
about_author: Cyrus Dravenmoor spent three years teaching at a boarding school he refuses to name, where he kept a private file of things students were never told. He writes young adult fiction about institutions, memory, and the kids who refuse to be footnotes.

chapters.title: The Counting Days
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Establishes Hollowmere Academy and Silas's survival strategy of invisibility as he counts down to graduation. A scholarship kid among legacies, he endures Wren Calloway's casual cruelty. Emotional beat: weary resignation cracked by a flicker of longing when he sees the old Homecoming banners in the gym rafters.

chapters.title: Assigned Seats
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Mr. Abernathy pairs Silas with Wren for the semester capstone: a documentary history of Hollowmere's Homecoming. Both protest; both are refused. Emotional beat: trapped fury curdling into reluctant curiosity when Wren admits she doesn't actually know why the town celebrates.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren negotiates brutal ground rules—no friendship, no questions about her family—and reveals her pressure to win the Founder's Prize like her mother did. Emotional beat: brittle control masking fear that she is only her surname.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In the basement archive they find yearbooks with pages razored out and a 1974 gap where no Homecoming happened. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by unease—the omissions feel deliberate, curated by someone still alive.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Interviews around Hollowmere yield cheerful, identical scripts about 'tradition' until a diner owner mentions 'the bad autumn' and goes silent. Emotional beat: growing sense that the whole town is performing a memory.

chapters.title: Fire Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds her grandmother's letters referencing a dormitory fire and four names no one will say. She hides them from Silas, ashamed of what her family may have buried. Emotional beat: guilt arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In a scorched ledger, Silas finds 'E. Voss' listed among the dead—possibly kin. His scholarship suddenly feels less like charity than hush money. Emotional beat: vertigo; his invisibility was engineered.

chapters.title: Detention as Research
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Caught sneaking into restricted stacks, both serve detention transcribing records for Headmaster Crane—who watches them too closely. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming under surveillance; first real laughter between them.

chapters.title: The Cancelation Notice
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The board announces this will be the final Homecoming, citing costs. The town applauds its own erasure. Emotional beat: outrage crystallizing into purpose—the project becomes a rescue mission.

chapters.title: Crane's Office
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crane offers Wren the Founder's Prize if their project stays 'celebratory.' She accepts, then hates herself. Emotional beat: temptation, betrayal foreshadowed, the prize as a leash.

chapters.title: Rift
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas discovers Wren's deal and the hidden letters. Their partnership shatters in the archive room. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deeper because it felt like belonging.

chapters.title: The Bad Autumn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV alone in the town library. She reconstructs the 1974 fire: four students died after being locked in during a prank gone wrong; the Calloway patriarch held the keys. Emotional beat: horror becoming resolve—she will not inherit silence.

chapters.title: Homecoming Week
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The last Homecoming proceeds as hollow pageantry while Silas and Wren work separately, gathering testimony from aging witnesses. Emotional beat: grief threaded through celebration; the town mourning without knowing why.

chapters.title: Threats
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas's scholarship is revoked effective graduation week; his dorm room is searched. Someone wants him gone before the anniversary date. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance—he has nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fourth victim wasn't Voss—it was a Calloway, disowned posthumously to protect the family. Wren realizes her legacy and Silas's exile are the same wound. Emotional beat: devastating recognition; she seeks him out.

chapters.title: Truce
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Silas and Wren reconcile over the complete evidence: letters, ledgers, photographs. They plan to present everything at the Homecoming assembly. Emotional beat: fragile trust rebuilt into something like friendship.

chapters.title: Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Crane locks the archive, confiscates their materials, and threatens expulsion. But Silas has already memorized the ledger and mailed copies to the diner owner and two retired teachers. Emotional beat: cornered but no longer alone.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the final Homecoming assembly, Wren takes the stage to accept the Founder's Prize—and instead reads the four names aloud. Emotional beat: terror transforming into liberation mid-sentence.

chapters.title: The Town Answers
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. One by one, townspeople stand and speak the names, adding memories Crane can't confiscate. The diner owner produces the mailed documents. Emotional beat: catharsis; a town remembering itself in public.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Crane resigns; the board restores Silas's scholarship and votes to make Homecoming a permanent memorial. Wren forfeits the Prize knowingly. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning—justice achieved outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: A Yearbook for the Homecoming
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They finish the project: a new yearbook restoring the missing pages, the four names printed where they were cut away. Emotional beat: tenderness; making something whole from what was torn.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, final chapter. Silas walks at graduation having chosen to stay in Hollowmere for college, no longer counting days. He and Wren hang the restored banner beside the old ones. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted—the sentence served becomes a home.
